anya: Quick thread — ran token-splice + headorder experiments between llm:llama-13b-v2 (fp16 baseline), gemma-7b-int4 (our quant build), and mistral-xx (float) on our eval harness. Noticed a consistent worst-case drop on instruction-following when we swap head order during conversion.

julia: what do you mean by 'swap head order'? model conversion step reordered attention heads?

anya: yeah. converter mapping used head_permute mapping from Llama layout -> Gemma layout. In conversion I applied permute_heads = [2,0,1,3] shorthand for head groups; suspicion is rotary phase alignment gets misapplied per-head. paste command and logs:

anya: ```
python tools/convert_model.py --src llama-13b --dst gemma-7b --perm-heads '2,0,1,3' --quant int4 --out out/gemma-7b-int4
# eval: 
python eval/hf_eval.py --model out/gemma-7b-int4 --task instructbench --seed 42 --batch 8
```

anya: eval summary (instructbench subset, 200 prompts):
- llama-13b (fp16): instr-succ 86.5% , sacrebleu 28.1
- gemma-7b-int4 (no perm): 82.2% , sacrebleu 26.9
- gemma-7b-int4 (perm applied): 70.4% , sacrebleu 19.7

raj: that's a huge drop. Did you check logits / topk overlap to see if it's semantic shift vs formatting?

anya: did. top1 overlap vs baseline (llama fp16):
- gemma int4 no perm: 0.77
- gemma int4 perm: 0.54
So it's not just tokenization; the model's next-token distribution is markedly different.

sienna: could be rotary phase mismatch per head — permuting heads without adjusting rotary sin/cos mapping would break relative phase alignment. Did converter reassign rotary params?

anya: converter attaches rotary tensors by head-index and just permutes q/k proj weights. I didn't modify rotary buffers. Quick test: zeroed rotary for last 4 layers -> perf recovers to 79% for perm run (was 70.4).

julia: interesting. so disabling rotary partially recovers. That points at headwise-phase issue. Can you dump a small attention weight and rotary cos matrix diff?

anya: pasted diffs (snippet):
```
layer 22, head 1 cos mean diff 0.0032
layer 22, head 3 cos mean diff 0.487
attention mean L2 diff (baseline vs perm): 0.12
```

raj: head 3 huge cos diff — perhaps head group stride mismatch during reshape (heads x head_dim). Do we still assume head_dim 128? any off-by-one in reshape dims when converting from gemma param layout?

anya: converter used inferred hd = weight.shape[-1] // num_heads, hd=64 for these models. But Gemma variant actually packs adapters so effective head_dim is 64 but index mapping differs (grouped). I think there's an interleaving step missing.

sienna: next steps I suggest:
1) add explicit rotary remap step: permute rotary buffers the same as q/k mappings
2) add sanity check script in convert pipeline that runs 20 prompts and computes top1 overlap vs src
3) log a warning when top1 overlap < 0.7

anya: implemented 1 & 2 locally, reran quick smoke: permute rotary buffers -> gemma-int4 perm: instr-succ 81.9% (close to 82.2). top1 overlap now 0.75. Will open PR with tests + short historical note.

ci-bench: run 6842 finished — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/1722223333-tokensplice/

julia: awesome. can you include a small test case in converters/test/ that asserts top1 overlap > 0.72 for any head perm steps? keep it non-blocking but flagged.

anya: yep will do. Also adding a converter flag --remap-rotary to keep backwards compat. opening draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/converter/pull/812 :slightly_smiling_face:

raj: nice. after PR merge let's run full 1k instructbench + a handful of long-context MMLU-style prompts to catch subtle degenerations.

sienna: also file a short onboarding note in the model catalog: "When converting between llama-like and gemma-like head layouts, ensure rotary buffers are remapped or disable head_permute during initial smoke tests."

anya: added to draft catalog entry. tl;dr: head-order permute WITHOUT rotary remap -> severe quality regression. Permute + remap -> ok. Will monitor quantized/rescaled kernels too.

julia: thanks for the triage. tagging @infra-ml to watch for CI noise: #eng-ml
